laws.rule: In the City of Dublin it is an offence to drink alcohol on a road (street, lane, footpath, square and similar) or in a public place under Dublin City Council's control, or to hold alcohol there intending to drink it or supply it for drinking there. Public places include parks, open spaces, beaches, the Liffey boardwalk, canal banks and towpaths, churchyards and the grounds of buildings the public can enter. The fine is up to EUR 1,900 (about A$3,019 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293) (Dublin City Council (Prohibition of Consumption of Intoxicating Liquor on Roads and in Public Places) Bye-Laws 2008, bye-law 6). A Garda or authorised person may tell you to stop and leave the area (bye-law 7), may ask your name and address (bye-law 8(a)), and a Garda may confiscate the alcohol and arrest without a warrant (8(b) and 8(c)). Drinking at tables and chairs a pub, hotel or restaurant provides on the street next to it, within its licence, is not an offence (bye-law 9). The council says the bye-laws are in force.
